question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of an ideal gas is allowed to expand isothermally into vacuum until the total volume is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math>. The amount of heat absorbed in this expansion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> atm.

solution.text:
In case of expansion, work is done by system.

Now, as we know that,

W=-Pext. ∆V

As the gas is expanding into vacuums which has no pressure, i.e.,

Pext.=0

∴ W=0

Hence, no work is done.

From first law of thermodynamics,

ΔU=q+W

As the system is working at constant temperature, i.e., isothermally.

∴ΔU=0

Hence q=-W=0
